title: Evaluation and quotient transitions of normalized system direct image
statement: For a prime l, a finite extension E of Q_l, a scheme map f:X→Y and any Direct d in [def-strict-coefficient-system-operation-data], there is a DirectEvaluation for d: its evaluation isomorphisms satisfy both adjunction equations, its restricted direct-image comparison is the specified sfDerivedImageRestriction, and its adjacent quotient transition equation holds. This concerns every derived system, without boundedness, cartesian or coefficient-invertibility hypotheses.

source.place: Strict-system realization: the construction argument recorded in lem-sf-integral-system-operation-models; Zheng Construction 4.1 and Lemma 4.10, Stacks 03DI, 09AE, 0E8I and 0941.

proof.text: Define β_n to be the right mate of the inverse of the fixed pullbackTensorDerivedEvaluation under d.adj and finiteAdj_n. It is invertible by the canonical evaluation mate lemma, so asIso β_n supplies the evaluation isomorphism.

The evaluated unit identity is unit_mateEquiv followed by the finite direct image of α_n.hom; functoriality cancels α_n.inv followed by α_n.hom. The counit identity is mateEquiv_counit followed by α_n.hom, cancelling α_n.hom followed by α_n.inv. These are proved in Lean without additional hypotheses or holed coherence statements.

Use originRestrictionEquality and proof irrelevance for the exactness instances to identify the derived quotient-restriction presentations. Transport sfDerivedImageRestriction across those equalities, retaining its heterogeneous equality; restrictedDirect_exists proves this normalization with no hole. Let δ be the inverse mate of its inverse. Apply the pullback quotient square. Naturality of mates with respect to top and bottom transformations and mateEquiv_vcomp transfer this square to the direct-image equation with an extra factor r.inv. Postcompose with r.hom and cancel r.inv followed by r.hom. This proves the full specified transition equation.
